status: DRAFT for Dan's review. Supersedes data/data_dictionary.csv, which is a glossary.

jobs: a structured test-statistic string such as F(2, 154) = 12.47
root_finding_polymorphic_columns.consequence: Every numeric rule silently skips the string cells, because parsing coerces them to null. They are invisible to every range check. And a CORRECT refusal to convert (F with df1>1 cannot become one correlation) is indistinguishable from a parse failure -- both leave es_r empty.
root_finding_polymorphic_columns.origin: Not corruption and not the AI: 294 of these declare es_type='test statistic', all are validated=yes, and all arrive from the FReD v2.4.2 June 2026 import. Keeping F(2,154)=12.47 verbatim is BETTER provenance than a bare 12.47. The defect is that one column stores two kinds of thing.
fix: es_value            float, the effect size only
test_statistic_type enum: t | F | chi2 | z

root_finding_polymorphic_columns.consequence: Two numbers in one string need a parser, and the parser is ambiguous: the cell '0.008-0.850' reads as lower 0.008, upper -0.850 because the hyphen is taken as a minus sign. That single ambiguity produced one of two reported inverted intervals and one of twelve reported containment failures -- both were parser bugs, not data defects.
root_finding_polymorphic_columns.origin: A display convention ('[lo, hi]') stored as data.
fix: es_ci_scale  enum: same_as_es | log -- 4 ratio rows store a LOG-scale interval against a ratio-scale estimate, which no containment check can currently detect

jobs: the comparator (= < >) when the paper reported a bound
the name of the statistical test
root_finding_polymorphic_columns.consequence: 307 cells hold test names or free text -- 't', 'chi-squared', 'genome-wide meta-analysis', 'cluster-wise corrected p (permutation test)'. Any check that recomputes p from an effect size and n assumes a two-tailed t, and this column is the only place the data says otherwise. I made exactly that error: I reported 18 rows as statistically inconsistent, and at most 2-4 survive once the declared test is respected.
root_finding_polymorphic_columns.origin: One column asked to describe two different aspects of a p-value.
fix: test_statistic_type enum, shared with the es split above
p_value_adjustment enum: none | bonferroni | fdr | permutation | cluster | other
p_value_tails enum: one | two  (currently five spellings for two concepts)

correlation.note: bounded by construction (a standardised covariance / cosine); |value|>1 impossible

standardised_mean_diff.note: unbounded signal-to-noise ratio; |d|>6 is possible but should be verified

paired_smd.note: d_z = mean difference / SD OF DIFFERENCES, so it depends on the within-subject correlation and is NOT on the between-groups d metric. The same true effect gives d_z from 0.21 (r=0) to 2.12 (r=0.99). Must not be converted with the between-groups formula, and must not be pooled with d.

ratio.note: strictly positive; <=0 is impossible. DIRECTIONAL, but the direction is position relative to 1, not sign. OR=0.33 is a negative effect and correctly converts to a NEGATIVE r -- 171 cells do exactly that and must not be flagged.

log_ratio.note: a LOG ratio (or a rate DIFFERENCE) is signed and unbounded, null 0. Negative whenever the treated group is lower. 86 of 190 log-ROM cells are negative; a positivity constraint here would quarantine correct data.

variance_share.note: a proportion of variance; outside [0,1] impossible, and it carries NO direction

nonneg_unbounded.soft_hi_note: phi and Cohen's w are bounded by sqrt(k-1) for a k x k table, so >1 is legal but needs the table dimensions to check. Flag, do not reject.
nonneg_unbounded.note: non-negative and unbounded; a negative value is impossible (3 w cells are negative)

cramers_v.note: V = sqrt(chi2 / (N * min(r-1, c-1))) -- a square root, so NEVER negative. It equals |phi| only for a 2x2 table; for anything larger it is not a Pearson r and MUST NOT be passed through to es_r.

probability_of_superiority.note: probability a random positive outranks a random negative. NULL IS 0.5, not 0. Converting via sqrt() -- the variance-share route -- turns a null AUC of 0.50 into r = 0.71. Correct route is d = sqrt(2) * Phi^-1(AUC).

uninterpretable_without_units.note: raw regression coefficients are in ARBITRARY UNITS and unbounded. Excluded from pooling and from es_r by construction. This is the same class of object as the 566.5 stored as a correlation.

values.reversal: a significant effect in the OPPOSITE direction
values.[proposed] informative_failure: FReD: the success condition is not met -- same direction but not significant, opposite-direction significant, or a null

a blank result with validated=yes is a contradiction (139 rows)
PROVENANCE GAP: add outcome_basis (author_statement | curator | ai)

MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS depending on original_claim_direction. The rule `if pOrig >= .05: return pRep >= .05 ? success : failure` drops the direction check that FReD requires, and assumes the original was seeking an effect. See the null-findings documentation draft.
'both non-significant = success' needs an EQUIVALENCE test, not p > .05. Two underpowered nulls agreeing is not confirmation.

cross_field_rules: replication_year >= original_year  [FLAG only -- preprints and registered reports break it]
if es_type is present then es or a test statistic must be present  [INFO, not error]
if family(es_type) == 'nonneg_unbounded' then es >= 0  [flag, do not reject, above 1]
if es_type in PASS_THROUGH then abs(es_r - es) <= 0.01
if family(es_type) is non-directional then es_r >= 0  [ratios EXCLUDED -- they are directional]
if family(es_type) == 'uninterpretable_without_units' then es_r must be NULL
es_ci_lower <= es_ci_upper, and the interval must contain es, WHEN es_ci_scale == same_as_es
the CI half-width must be within 3x of what es and n imply
a CI excluding the null implies p < 0.05  [use this INSTEAD of recomputing p from es_r]
result must not contradict the row's own p-value and effect-size signs
quarantine_policy: A row failing a rule goes to a quarantine table WITH THE RULE ID and is excluded from published figures until resolved. Never silently dropped, never silently passed. A rule that fires on legitimate data is worse than no rule, because it gets the whole gate switched off -- four rules in the previous revision did exactly that.
